Pfenninger, Finneron, Melchior and Sutton have done much to help our Field Events along, and Vallance may become a first-class pole vaulter in due course.

Jones represented us in the Kinnaird Trophy hurdles, but were drawn in heats with Finlay and Pilbrow respectively, and so were unable to qualify for the final. At this meeting Sutton (35 ft. 8 ins.) and S. Jones (34 ft. 11½ ins.) represented us in the Shot Putt.

Second points were scored on our behalf by Abberton (Mile), Quackenbos (High Jump), Murdoch (880 yards), Sutton (Shot), and single points for third places came from Johns (220 yards and 100 yards), Lucas (Mile), Blyther (High Jump), Taylor (880 yards), F.
As usual, our Field Events men acquitted themselves well, and added to our points. Grassau was responsible for the best Shot Putt of the day, and with Mechior, Sutton and T.

Once again we have a likely lot of "Juniors" and from their numbers it should be possible to find a team capable of winning once again if only they will train steadily and regularly, and not spasmodically. Names that come to the mind are Speechley, Sutton, Storey, R.

A "B" team, consisting of Boddington, Clark, Cornish, Martin, Snell, Reeve and Sutton also started. From the start our walkers were prominent, together with those of Surrey W.C. and Leicester W.C.—the three teams securing the placings in last year's race.
Jack Bidgood and Colin Sutton were walking well together for our third scoring position. After 4 laps (with 6¼ miles to go), M.W.C. had a 4 point advantage.

Fred's time was, however, within a few seconds of his previous best, and his wonderfully fine performance at 39 years of age should inspire many of our younger members. Our next to finish, in eleventh position, was Colin Sutton. He completed the course in 8h. 49m. 40s.—a wonderfully fine first attempt.
Sutton completing the team. Although we won two of the three events, we lost the match on the aggregate., points being Belgrave 29, Met.
Sutton. All are certain to show a high standard of performance, and we have hopes of supplying the individual champion.

The Club Championship found a new holder, Colin Sutton being first man home. He walked with both power and speed, and although a very tired man towards the finish, he lasted home and showed that we have another first-class distance walker in our ranks.
Sutton, F.
Doubleday is another to have changed over and shows great promise; while in Colin Sutton we have one who has competed with some distinction in cycling road races.

Under the able captaincy of Bill Sutton, our Field Events men are once again giving a good account of themselves. In Southern Amateur Athletic League events, with thirteen events decided, we have scored 148 points out of a possible 156.
Our great hope was Colin Sutton. Unfortunately, a severe cold laid him low a week before the race, necessitating a day in bed, but Colin started in this race as though in perfect health.
Sutton and Reg Elson completed the team,
London Associated Electrical Undertakings. Sutton won the Shot Putt, T.

The judges soon got to work, for Colin Sutton was disqualified when he had only covered about a quarter of a mile. After a small lap of the Common, Harry was already in front, and Belgrave vests were already prominent.

Open Walk, originally postponed owing to frozen roads, was held on March 9th, and gave us another very easy team win. Our first man home was Jack Rutland, in third position; and the other team men were Coleman 5, Sutton 9, and C.
In the mile, Bill Lucas had a grand tussle with Bingham, T.C.C., who won by a few yards in 4m 32 secs., Cohen finishing 3rd. In the field events, Sutton and Jones upheld the club's prestige.

Bill Sutton also did well in taking second place in the Discus and third in the Weight. The Javelin was won by the ever-green George Pownell, who is still showing the youngsters how to throw a javelin correctly.
Bill Sutton was second in the Weight and also gained third place in the Discus, but Bill seems to miss the support of Syd Jones, our other " strong " man, who is in the Services.
We were very glad to welcome Syd Jones in the Weight, and he won with a fine put of 38ft. 11in. Bill Sutton took second place, with D.
Bill Sutton is finding Italy to his liking and has found a good billet with good food (nice work!). Spent a night in the mountains and enjoyed a fall of snow.
Heartiest Congratulations to Colin Sutton and Jock Martin upon their performances in the 24 Hours' Walk, held at the White City on July 14th-15th.

Those to have finished the distance inside 9 hours and excluding the performances just quoted are Bellchamber (twice), Miles, Rathbone, Bentley, Martin (R.) (4 times), Bidgood (3 times), Rickards (twice), Urry (twice), Sutton (twice), Baker and Stirling Wakeley.

…ne most pleasant surprise of the day was the return of two of our best and most popular distance walkers, namely, Colin Sutton, just returned from Australia looking very brown and fit, and Fred Rickards, who informed us he was going to make a comeback, not looking quite so brown, but fitter and, if…
In the 2 miles walk we saw our old friend Colin Sutton getting among the prizes once again and his trip abroad has evidently not impaired his speed.

We have had a number of placed men - Tommy Green on three occasions - but never a winner. Here's a target for next year; to beat our 1938 winning team score of 23 points (Bentley 2, Sutton 4, Bidgood 8 Rickards 9)!
